title: Universe-small model for quasi-representable dg functors
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal J,\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal U$-small dg categories over $\mathbf Z$, with dg categories, $H^0$, quasi-equivalences, the localization $\mathsf{Hqe}$, and a $\mathcal U$-small cofibrant replacement $Q\mathcal J\to\mathcal J$ as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. Write $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal U}$ for cochain complexes of $\mathcal U$-small abelian groups. Form the full dg category $\mathcal R$ of covariant dg functors $T:Q\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)_{\mathcal U}$ which are homotopically projective as modules over $(Q\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ and whose fibers $T(j,-)$ are isomorphic in the derived category of right $\mathcal B$-modules to representables $\mathcal B(-,b_j)$. Module Hom complexes and homotopical projectivity use [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution]; tensor, opposite, and the right quasi-representable condition use [lem-coef-dgcat-bimodule-mapping-space]. Then $\mathcal R$ has $\mathcal U$-small morphism complexes and admits a $\mathcal U$-small full dg subcategory $\mathcal R_0$ with one representative of each $H^0$-isomorphism class. Its inclusion is a quasi-equivalence, and the $H^0$-isomorphism classes of $\mathcal R_0$ are naturally indexed by $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal J,\mathcal B)$.

source.place: Toën, Corollary 4.11 and its proof, using Corollary 4.8; homotopically projective variant uses the module model in Section 3. No Stacks tag states this dg-category result; read online, not archived in literature/.

proof.text:
Put $D=Q\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its objects are pairs and its morphism complexes are tensors of the given small complexes, so $D$ is $\mathcal U$-small. For $T,T'\in\mathcal R$, degree $r$ of their module Hom is a subgroup of
$$\prod_{x\in\operatorname{Ob}D}\prod_{n\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(T(x)^n,T'(x)^{n+r}),$$
cut out by the graded module-action equations. Each factor is a subset of a function set between two $\mathcal U$-small sets. Closure of a Grothendieck universe under function sets, small products and subsets makes this subgroup $\mathcal U$-small. The differential and composition are restrictions of the specified Hom differential and composition. Thus all morphism complexes of $\mathcal R$ are $\mathcal U$-small, even though its object collection need only be $\mathcal V$-small.

source.place: Toën, Corollaries 4.8 and 4.11, printed pp. 28-29; Section 3, Proposition 3.5, printed p. 15. Read online; agent expansion for homotopically projective modules and explicit universe bounds.

proof.text: Apply the projective-resolution theorem to right $D^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules with $\mathcal U$-small values, keeping their category in $\mathcal V$. It supplies, within this module category, a homotopically projective replacement $P\to M$ of every such module and identifies $H^0$ of its full projective dg category with the ordinary derived localization, compatibly with composition. Restrict to the right quasi-representable objects. Restriction to a fiber preserves objectwise quasi-isomorphisms; hence if $M(j,-)$ is derived-isomorphic to a representable, so is $P(j,-)$. Therefore this restriction is essentially surjective onto all right quasi-representable objects of the derived localization. It is fully faithful because the projective-resolution theorem computes derived maps by the actual Hom complex between projectives. Consequently two objects of $\mathcal R$ have the same derived isomorphism class exactly when they are isomorphic in $H^0\mathcal R$.

source.place: Toën, Corollaries 4.8 and 4.11, printed pp. 28-29; Section 3, Proposition 3.5, printed p. 15. Read online; agent expansion for homotopically projective modules and explicit universe bounds.

proof.text:
Use the connected-component assertion of the bimodule mapping-space theorem with $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)=(\mathcal J,\mathcal B)$ and the stipulated $Q\mathcal J$. It identifies all right quasi-representable $D$-modules in the derived localization, with no fiberwise cofibrancy restriction, with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal J,\mathcal B)$. Combining it with Step 2 gives a bijection
$$\operatorname{Iso}(H^0\mathcal R)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal J,\mathcal B).$$
In particular we have not assumed that an arbitrary homotopically projective bimodule has cofibrant fibers; the cited theorem explicitly omits that condition for this isomorphism-class assertion.

source.place: Toën, Corollaries 4.8 and 4.11, printed pp. 28-29; Section 3, Proposition 3.5, printed p. 15. Read online; agent expansion for homotopically projective modules and explicit universe bounds.

proof.text: The right-hand side of Step 3 is essentially $\mathcal U$-small. Indeed the dg-category model theorem represents every one of its morphisms by a strict dg functor $Q\mathcal J\to\mathcal B$, since $Q\mathcal J$ is cofibrant and every dg category is fibrant; precomposition with its quasi-equivalence to $\mathcal J$ is invertible in the localization. The strict functors form a $\mathcal U$-small set: choose an object function between the two small object sets, then a family of chain maps between their morphism complexes; functoriality cuts out a subset of this small product of function sets. Their quotient by equality in the localization is still $\mathcal U$-small. The universe-enlargement assertion of the same theorem ensures that computing the localization in $\mathcal V$ does not enlarge these morphisms.

source.place: Toën, Corollaries 4.8 and 4.11, printed pp. 28-29; Section 3, Proposition 3.5, printed p. 15. Read online; agent expansion for homotopically projective modules and explicit universe bounds.

proof.text: Choose a $\mathcal U$-small set $I$ indexing the classes in Step 4 and, using Step 3, choose one actual object $T_i\in\mathcal R$ in each corresponding class. This is choice over a set in $\mathcal V$. Each $T_i$ is encoded by $\mathcal U$-small data: a family of complexes indexed by the small object set of $D$, and action maps indexed by pairs of objects and integer degrees. All these families belong to $\mathcal U$ by closure under small indexed products and unions. Hence the set of chosen representatives is $\mathcal U$-small as well. Let $\mathcal R_0$ be the full dg subcategory on precisely these objects. Step 1 makes its morphism complexes small, and its differential, compositions and units are inherited by fullness; thus $\mathcal R_0$ is a $\mathcal U$-small dg category.

source.place: Toën, Corollaries 4.8 and 4.11, printed pp. 28-29; Section 3, Proposition 3.5, printed p. 15. Read online; agent expansion for homotopically projective modules and explicit universe bounds.

proof.text: For any chosen pair $T_i,T_{i'}$, the inclusion $\mathcal R_0\hookrightarrow\mathcal R$ induces the identity of the actual module Hom complexes, hence a quasi-isomorphism. Every object of $H^0\mathcal R$ is isomorphic to its chosen representative by Step 5. These are exactly the quasi-fully faithful and essentially surjective conditions in the definition of a quasi-equivalence. The inclusion is therefore a quasi-equivalence.

source.place: Toën, Corollaries 4.8 and 4.11, printed pp. 28-29; Section 3, Proposition 3.5, printed p. 15. Read online; agent expansion for homotopically projective modules and explicit universe bounds.

proof.text: The map on $H^0$-isomorphism classes induced by this full inclusion is bijective: it is surjective by the representative choice, and any isomorphism between two representatives already lies in the full subcategory. Compose its bijection with that of Step 3 to obtain the asserted indexing. This indexing is independent of the representative choice because it sends a representative to the derived isomorphism class of that very same bimodule. The bimodule theorem says the latter classification commutes with restriction in the source and derived extension in the target. Replacing the resulting module by a homotopically projective one leaves its derived class unchanged by Step 2. Thus the indexing is natural on isomorphism classes for these operations; no functorial choice of a strict skeleton is required.

I also read the full statements of the four cited nodes: dgcat-model-structure, dg-module-projective-resolution, dgcat-bimodule-mapping-space and def-weil-size-convention. Toën math/0408337 is not in literature/, so I fetched it from arXiv and read it there: §3 (Prop 3.2-3.5 and the Int(M) definition with its U-small Hom complexes, pp.13-15), Def 4.1, the remark before Cor 4.8 that dropping fiber cofibrancy changes nothing, and Cor 4.8, 4.9 and 4.11 with proof (pp.27-29). Variance matches the source: covariant functors on QJ⊗B^op, with fibers that are right B-modules. Step-by-step: S1 bounds Hom complexes inside the universe by elementary closure. S2 uses the resolution node: an h-projective replacement restricts to fiber quasi-isomorphisms, so quasi-representability survives, and full faithfulness is H0 of the derived Hom. S3 is exactly the bimodule node's connected-component clause, which states it holds without the cofibrancy condition. S4 rests on strict functors from the cofibrant QJ into the fibrant B, a U-small set whose quotient is U-small. S5-S6 choose representatives, build the full subcategory and show the inclusion is a quasi-equivalence, using Step 3 injectivity for essential surjectivity. S7 gets naturality on classes by restriction or extension followed by replacement; it does not claim a strict skeleton. Edge cases all match: empty J gives one class; nonempty J with empty B gives the empty set on both sides; B the zero category gives one class; J the unit category gives iso classes of [B] (Cor 4.9). No duplicate turned up in an rg search for quasi-representable, small-subcategory and 4.11 terms. The item is not a restated parent clause, since the parent lem-coef-dg-quasifunctor-invariance only uses it in one step, and it introduces no cycle. All cited nodes are in the same unit, so no tool_uses are needed. No SGA is used and this is not a target node. The blueprint ancestry is unchanged. There are no new nodes and no fixes. One reading I relied on, not counted as a fault: the resolution node's replacement stays in the module category with U-small values.
